description: The floating-point numeric literal (ISO §2023:8.3.3.3.3: 'A floating-point numeric literal is formed from two fixed-point numeric literals separated by the letter E without intervening spaces'; the DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA spelling 1,5E3 is the same literal, §2023:12.3.7.4 GR14 a) - 1.5E3, -2.5E-2, .5E10 - in every position the lexer produces one (COMPUTE operand, MOVE source, VALUE, relation operand, FUNCTION argument, subscript, SET, CALL argument). A different construct from the floating-point USAGEs (usage-float-short-2002, usage-float-binary32-2014 ...) and from the floating-point numeric-edited PICTURE (pic-external-float-2002), which are data descriptions: the literal needs neither and appears in a program whose data are all fixed-point. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965), and is no longer provisional: §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.2 'A numeric literal is a character-string whose characters are selected from the digits '0' through '9', the plus sign, the minus sign, and the decimal point.' - the fixed-point form alone; §2002:8.3.1.2.2.2 'A floating-point numeric literal is formed from two fixed-point numeric literals separated by the letter 'E' without intervening spaces.', which §2014:8.3.1.2.2.2 prints word for word, and §2014:E.3 item 20 raises the significand of 'a floating-point literal' from 31 to 36 digits - a change to a literal 2002 already had (VCR row 7.37). None of the 459 NIST CCVS-85 programs writes one. Gated position-blind on the TOKEN by LiteralScreen (kb/Work PB674), whose walk covers the unit's tree and every compiler-directive fragment.
